newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Talk of Duff & Phelps rating lifts S.African bonds.
newsitem.headline: Talk of Duff & Phelps rating lifts S.African bonds.

text.p: Talk of a bullish rating from U.S. agency Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co helped lift South African debt on Wednesday, dealers said.
South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel implied earlier in Tokyo that the country would get an investment grade rating for its upcoming Yankee bond issue from Duff & Phelps.
"We can access a wider array of capital sources in the United States, and we think this is good for South Africa's future Yankees," he told reporters.
A spokeswoman for Duff & Phelps in London confirmed that South Africa had been considered by a committee on Tuesday but said no statement had yet been issued.
A South African finance ministry official said a Duff & Phelps delegation had visited South Africa at the end of May.
Manuel and his finance team -- currently in Tokyo to promote a 40 billion yen samurai issue -- are expected to go to New York shortly for a roadshow to launch a Yankee bond.
Market talk suggests the Yankee, for which Merrill Lynch is lead manager, could be about $500 million with a 20-year maturity.
Officials say the Yankee and samurai issues together are expected to complete the country's foreign borrowing target of four billion rand for 1997/98 (April-March).

South Africa's long-term debt currently straddles investment grade. Moody's Investor's Services already rates the country an investment prospect at Baa3, but Standard and Poor's ranks it one notch below at BB+, though with a positive outlook.
